notes: Suites full-cold and full-warm ran at 7f2ca9e and full-references-none at b51b48b; both are runtime-identical to 2761eb14 (only AGENTS.md and docs differ).
The inventory, workflows and seeded runs read the clean main checkout at 2761eb1 or runtime-identical commits; corpus and test hashes agree across those runs.

Both builds ran at d9beb57 (runtime-identical) and reproduced the 7f2ca9e build byte for byte. Exports and captures loaded those cached files; character-view/ and examples/ are unchanged from 2761eb14 through 0b41842, so the forms opened were the reference forms (export.json records each form SHA-256).

The shared desktop-port-guidance checkout moved to the pnpm workspace (3a9a07d onwards) during the per-module timing, and modules after the 81st ran while the GPU export used the CPU. Treat observed.moduleTimings as indicative; the full-suite cold and warm times were measured on an idle machine.

Reproduced with run-g0.mjs --quick --skip-suite from a clean detached worktree at 2761eb1 after npm ci: identical build hashes, seeded digest, corpus and test hashes; 12/12 quick exports match the frozen content digests and 29/29 tracked-GLB shots match the frozen r0 captures byte for byte.

Evidence pass on 2026-11-25 after independent review: inventory.json and workflows.json were regenerated with the extended scripts in a clean CRLF clone of 2761eb14 (the earlier files are kept as *.44a4a93.json; every earlier field matched except the CR left in licence titles). Captures and exports were not rerun: compare.py pixels decoded all 1,464 retained frames, compare.py reencode re-encoded the 848 r0 frames, eol.mjs inventoried and built LF and CRLF clones, browser.py flows drove the offline AI tab and hybrid forms on the frozen build, and references.mjs plus browser.py references ran on a scratch clone of 2761eb14 holding local copies of the ignored reference sets.

findings: Fresh exports repeat in content: 245/245 share the content digest and 245/245 the decoded image pixels across a forward and a reverse run, but only 173/245 are byte-identical. The embedded images are identical; GLTFExporter writes them into the binary buffer in encode-completion order, so bufferView order and file hash vary. Identify artifacts by file hash and compare parity by content digest and pixels.
The editor's Open form rejects creature-dispatch.form.json and creature-pelt.form.json ("Choose a saved form."): they lack the irudd.form.v1 envelope. Their exports come from wrapped copies.

Tracked GLBs come from earlier builds: 0/31 match the fresh Game export's structure. 28 differ in image count and 1 in clip list; relay-concert.glb has no source form. Use them as playback fixtures and the fresh exports as export expectations.
Provenance: 2/32 tracked GLBs and 8/245 fresh exports carry asset.copyright; none carry asset.extras. The build embeds the asset credit in the HTML only.
Artwork: 52 blobs in 25 forms, all content-addressed as <role>-<sha256 of bytes> (52 match).
Seeded generators are deterministic across processes (digest 633fea957729ab31); entropy enters at 19 UI seed-draw sites and 10 revision-id/time sites.
Same-machine capture repeatability: 615/616 tracked-GLB shots and 540/540 fresh-export shots byte-identical; worst difference 1 level on 0.00009 % of pixels.

Changed captures: festival-wardrobe/portrait-side.png in repeat r1 (r0 and r2 agree), 1 pixel(s) off by up to 1 level against r0. Every retained frame is a RGB PNG. Against r0, 615/616 tracked and 540/540 fresh repeats have the same file hash and 615 and 540 the same pixel digest, so Chrome's PNG encoding was itself repeatable here.

PNG re-encoding (Pillow 12.2.0, compression 1 and 9) of all 848 r0 frames changes the file hash of 848 (level 1) and 848 (level 9) and keeps width, height, mode and pixel digest for 848 and 848. Compare captures by the decoded record; the file hash only identifies the retained Chrome frame.

Motion coverage is thin: each GLB's motion sample is its first clip at 50 % of the timeline, which is idle-0.5 for every GLB, and 25/32 tracked and 30/60 fresh motion shots are pixel-identical to the rest three-quarter shot.

Line endings: working-tree hashes follow core.autocrlf. 196/230 inventoried files hash differently in an LF and a CRLF clone of 2761eb14, while every gitBlob and canonicalSha256 agrees. The frozen sha256 values and build hashes come from a CRLF (Windows default) checkout; an LF clone builds character-view.html bd84b95a831a… and play-model.html 086af52db5e7…, because the bundle embeds the checkout's text bytes. Compare corpora by the canonical pair.

Private references switch on 7 practice rigs, 7 "3D reference fits" studies (52 → 66 studies), the Forms link (0 → 1) and dist/rig-study.html, which #compare-mhr opens from file://. WORKSHOP_REFERENCES=none in the same checkout rebuilds the public hashes (true).

Exports of an MHR fit carry asset.extras {referenceRigs, license}; the license is the build's docs/licenses/mhr-apache-2.0.txt text (equal to its working-tree sha256; LF-normalised it equals the canonical hash). The Lee Perry-Smith fit carries {referenceRigs, headScan} with the CC BY 3.0 credit, and both credits appear in asset.copyright.

Offline AI tab (no provider, no workshop-agent meta): Generate exports form-request.json ("Request exported. Ask your agent to return the proposal as JSON."); a stale proposal is refused ("This proposal belongs to a different request or an earlier edit."); an echo proposal opens for review ("Review the proposed form."); Inspect export reports "Inspect the pose and silhouette, then refine the proposal."; two refinement rounds export requests carrying the inspected views, the second adds the earlier-versus-current sheets (true); Accept → "AI variation accepted.", Discard → "Returned to the current form. Your nudge is still editable.". An attached image travels in the next request (1 reference).

Hybrid starting forms generate in the editor (seed 354601328: 22 parts, seed 780967474: 48 parts, seed 3782809234: 39 parts); each saved form reopens and re-exports with the same content digest (3/3).
gaps: Agent workflows (/variation, /turnaround, /trace-map, /portrait-depth) launch a Codex job per request, so G0 does not run them. recipe.test.js drives /variation through workshopServer with a stub worker; no test module covers scripts/codex-worker.mjs, scripts/art-direction.mjs, and the other three routes are not exercised. browser.py flows drives the offline half of each AI-tab flow instead.

Reference painting needs the workshop agent: Paint is hidden in the offline editor (verified) and character-view/art-variation.js, character-view/paint-sources.js, character-view/reuse-paint-editor.js have no test module; only reference-mask.js and reference-depth.js have unit tests. Painting is not frozen.

Hybrid starting forms need loaded turnarounds, so Node cannot generate them (seeded.mjs records 'Choose a loaded turnaround.' for every seed). The editor draws the seed itself, so browser.py flows freezes three drawn hybrids by their recorded seeds, not fixed seeds.

The suite and the frozen build are the public configuration. The private configuration was frozen from local copies of the ignored sets: Momentum Human Rig, rest pose installed; Six MHR benchmark bodies installed; Benchmark fits and pictures partial; Workshop fits to the six bodies partial; Scan preview studies partial; Scanned head fits installed; Rocketbox dressed avatars absent. Pages that need the missing pictures or Rocketbox are not covered.
Captures are single-machine (RTX 5070 Ti, ANGLE D3D11, Chrome headless). Cross-machine tolerance needs a second machine.
